fr:title.text: Porting the cubical library to build under Mikan

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Porting the cubical library to build under Mikan

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Got the full cubical library to type-check under Mikan (1lab's Agda fork; executable mikan, built from the flake, a mostly drop-in replacement for cubical Agda with a smaller feature set). Build with mikan -j --build-library from the repo root — -j/-j0 enables parallel checking, and the build stops at the first error (exit 42). Final state: exit 0, zero errors, with nothing commented out — every break turned out to be properly fixable.

The single most important gap: Mikan's termination checker only tracks structural descent across a changing index, not a changing data-type parameter. This breaks accessibility- and W-type-style recursion. The fix is uniformly to convert the recursive datatype's changing parameter into an index (the constructor interface and all use sites are unchanged). This also repairs recursions that go through transport/toPathP — the transport is never the real blocker, the parameter is. Applied to Acc (see well-founded recursion), IW, and DeepMonicPresentation.

html:ul.html:li: Reflection arg-info carries only Visibility — no modality/relevance/quantity. Drop the R.modality R.relevant R.quantity-ω argument.
Reflection's Type synonym is renamed Type' (because Type is now the universe). Use the portable R.Term, and hiding (Type') on unqualified opens.
No Agda.Builtin.Word / word64 literal — drop the import and the literal case.
Copattern projection won't resolve when the field name is shadowed by an open Record instance applied value — qualify it as .Record.field.
A record method defined by copattern that builds the same record inside the record body is rejected — lift it to a top-level definition taking the record value explicitly.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Caveat for any non-fixable breakage: Mikan enforces --safe imports (CoInfectiveImport), so dropping --safe or adding a terminating pragma cascades to every safe importer. Comment a broken definition out only after confirming nothing in the build references it.

fr:title.text: Parser by Well-Founded Recursion on String Length

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Parser by Well-Founded Recursion on String Length

fr:mainmatter.html:p: for every G : CFGDesc, where Parser A B (from Parser.Base) packages a splitting string ⊢ A ⊕ B with a disjointness witness disjoint A B.
Construction, by induction on input length:

html:ol.html:li: If the input is ε, answer by decidable nullability: G is nullable ⟹ inhabit ⟦ G ⟧cfg, otherwise inhabit the rejection side.

If the input is c ∷ w, recursively parse (δ c G) w via the syntactic derivative. Using ⟜ as derivative, a positive answer ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg w reshapes to ⟦ G ⟧cfg (c ∷ w); a negative answer ¬ ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg w lifts to ¬ ⟦ G ⟧cfg (c ∷ w).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Well-foundedness: on each recursive call length w strictly decreases. The grammar may grow (derivatives of CFGs are unbounded), but the well-founded relation is on the input, not the state. This mirrors how GCD.<₂-wellFounded in the intrinsically-recursive paper is well-founded on proj₂ of the index, not on the full index.
Concretely, the recursion uses <-wellFounded on ℕ via Cubical.Induction.WellFounded (already imported by the project's dependency on agda-stdlib).

This tree defines the algorithm operationally. The next step, parser as c2a-morphism, reinterprets the same definition as a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism, so the correctness proof becomes a uniqueness argument rather than a direct induction.
Milestone: implement this first for a hand-rolled Dyck (bypassing CFGDesc for the moment) to shake out the ⟜/nullability gymnastics before trying to generalise.
